newsitem.title: UK: Virgin's Branson offers smoke-free sponsorship.
newsitem.headline: Virgin's Branson offers smoke-free sponsorship.

text.p: Virgin Group boss Richard Branson said on Monday his companies would sponsor sports that lost any funding from tobacco companies.

He told a "smoking summit" in London that his group of companies would be happy to take over sponsorship if the government went ahead with a proposed ban on tobacco sponsorship of sports and the arts.
"I pledge today that Virgin will set up a rival spectacle, if necessary world-wide. And that goes for any sport that claims it cannot survive without cigarette advertising," Branson said.

"Even an international sport like the Grand Prix need not suffer," he added. "The only reason it is heavily sponsored by cigarette companies is that they are so desperate to reach a young TV audience, they have priced everyone else out of the market."
British health officials held the one-day summit to hear from experts around the country and from Europe, Australia and the United States.
Some worries had been voiced that sports and the arts would suffer from such a ban. Branson said the motor racing industry did not need the money -- but he would make it up if necessary.
"If this industry threatens to pull out of Silverstone -- and motor racing in Europe -- I, for one, will take them up on their bluff," Branson said.
Branson, himself an ex-smoker, praised the newly elected Labour government for its plans to ban cigarette advertising and limit smoking.

"Don't misunderstand me -- I am a libertarian," Branson said. "If adults, properly informed of its dangers, are foolish enough to want to fly around the world in a balloon and potentially kill themselves, they should be allowed to do so. Equally if adults want to smoke and buy cigarettes they also have the right, provided they don't cause harm to others."
But he said children did not know better. He proposed raising the legal age to buy cigarettes to 18 from 16 and said cigarettes should not be sold on open display. -- London Newsroom 44 171 542 8958
